cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Vertically integrated closed-system model. The Truenat platform (Trueprep extraction device + Truelab analyzer) is a closed system designed to work exclusively with the Company's own disease-specific Truenat test kits, so every installed device generates recurring consumable demand; new tests can be added to the installed base through a remote software update. 'Our vertical integration strategy allows us to bring healthcare innovations to market rapidly by streamlining the process from R&D to production, sales, and marketing. Through this approach, we combine design expertise, regulatory capabilities, and production know-how.' Backward into technology and product creation: R&D is done in-house through wholly-owned Subsidiary Bigtec Private Limited (incorporated 2000, wholly-owned since 2015; Bengaluru unit recognised by DSIR); 13 years of R&D preceded ICMR certification; 16 patents, 29 trademarks, 11 designs and 3 copyrights registered in India and 191 patents in foreign jurisdictions, with 7 patents and 10 designs applied for in India and 15 patents abroad. R&D team of 153 permanent employees including 136 scientists as of March 31, 2026; R&D spend Rs 8,745.6 lakhs / Rs 6,856.9 lakhs / Rs 5,977.7 lakhs, being 6.05% / 6.72% / 7.15% of revenue from operations in FY26/FY25/FY24. Manufacturing is in-house across six owned-operation (leased-land) facilities covering devices, chips, cartridges and reagents, with EMS vendors used only to assemble Truenat devices as and when required to meet demand. Forward integration into the screening pathway via acquisitions: Prognosys (65.47%, March 2023) adds ultraportable X-ray screening ahead of the confirmatory molecular test, plus the ProDigi/Tele-Rad digital health layer and mobile healthcare units; OptraScan (19.68% November 2024 rising to 60.00% via a second tranche on November 1, 2025) adds digital pathology scanning and telepathology. Not integrated upstream into raw materials: principal inputs are substrates, primers and probes, enzymes, dNTP, electronic components and chemicals, procured on individual purchase orders with no long-term supply contracts; certain materials are imported from South Korea, Switzerland, Denmark and Singapore, substrates come exclusively from a single supplier, and the top 10 suppliers accounted for 58.52% / 58.21% / 58.52% of purchases of raw materials and components consumed. Cost of raw material and components consumed was 46.66% / 52.99% / 48.63% of total expenses in FY26/FY25/FY24. Third-party logistics providers handle road and sea transport (freight 1.51% / 1.74% / 1.35% of total expenses).

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Revenue depends on Indian Central and State government and aid agency public healthcare programs procured through competitive tenders; unfavourable policy changes or a decrease in funding for those programs would directly reduce product sales, and payment cycles from public health programs are long, lifting working capital needs
- The loss of any of these customers or a decline in their demand would have an adverse effect on business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows; there is limited diversification to absorb the loss of a single large tender
- The economics rest on one disease programme; the intended expansion into an additional 34 assays for 22 diseases is unproven, so any shift in TB programme funding, protocol or competitive technology has an outsized effect
- No long-term supply contracts are in place (purchase orders are placed from time to time) for enzymes, primers, probes, electronic components and chips; import restrictions, embargoes or duty increases would hit margins, and raw material cost is already 46.66% of total expenses
- Working Capital Days of 166, 173 and 187 in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024; working capital loans of Rs 1,801.94 million as of March 31, 2026; non-current borrowings rose from Rs 61.44 million (March 31, 2025) to Rs 2,124.06 million (March 31, 2026) and current borrowings from Rs 1,170.19 million to Rs 2,002.32 million, while total liabilities rose from Rs 4,942.70 million to Rs 8,396.48 million
- Fiscal 2026 utilisation was 42.30% for devices and 58.25% for test kits (Fiscal 2025: 58.89% and 43.44%; Fiscal 2024: 19.83% and 27.45%); the Prognosys X-ray line ran at 50.71% and the Pune digital pathology line at 27.50%, so fixed manufacturing costs are spread over well below installed capacity and further capex is proposed from the Net Proceeds
- The core micro-PCR intellectual property sits with Subsidiary Bigtec and is licensed to the Company against royalty of 10% of revenue from operations (Fiscal 2026 royalty expense Rs 1,233.62 million) plus a security deposit of up to Rs 2,000.00 million; the 15-year term from August 1, 2011 was extended by only one year with effect from August 1, 2026 pursuant to an addendum dated July 25, 2026
- Pending direct and indirect tax claims of Rs 507.81 million (11 cases) against the Company and Rs 191.79 million (7 cases) against Subsidiaries; contingent liabilities as at March 31, 2026 include bank guarantees of Rs 900.98 million, direct tax disputes of Rs 461.48 million and indirect tax disputes of Rs 322.37 million; the Statutory Auditors' reports for Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 include an emphasis of matter paragraph, modifications and certain qualifications under the reporting on other legal and regulatory requirements
